title: Smoky Date and Bavarian Mustard Glaze
description: Soft dates give this mild mustard barbecue glaze a caramel flavor without a long reduction.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

ingredients.name: pitted Medjool dates
ingredients.note: Weigh after pitting, check for pit fragments and chop.

steps.title: Poach the dates
steps.text: Simmer {dates}, {broth} and {garlic} in the covered HexClad for 6–9 minutes until the dates can be mashed with a spoon.

steps.title: Blend the mustard glaze
steps.text: Blend the dates and their broth with {mustard} and {smoke}. Press the puree through a fine sieve into the skillet to remove date skins and coarse mustard seeds.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the finished sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup total. If it measures short, whisk in a little hot water. If it measures over, return it to the skillet and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Brush the warm glaze over pulled pork already moistened with gravy, or stir a spoonful into a serving of chicken braising sauce.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. One serving is 2 tablespoons. Make ahead: Pit and chop the dates a day ahead. Keep them covered and refrigerated until needed. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze for up to 2 months in small portions. The smooth date base thickens again as it reheats. Fridge reheat: Bring a portion to a boil in a small pan, stirring until it reaches at least 165°F. Loosen with a little water as needed. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses sweet mustard and smoked paprika. For gentler Option B, halve the mustard, leave out the paprika and finish with a little finely minced parsley. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 24 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 5.5 g total carbohydrate, 0.2 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 5 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
